title: db_integration_test.zig TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 still fail under concurrent `zig build test-integration`: test_iss503_rls_removal.zig's TC-ISS503-01/02/03 re-execute GBL-084's raw, unscoped guard/DDL against the shared public.tenant table in their own uncommitted transactions, colliding with concurrently-running binaries
notes:
Discovered by TEST-RUNNER during Step 5 final re-verification of ISS-0100's rework (GitHub #357, run WF03-iss0100-20260731). After ISS-0100's original fix (13 files + GBL-102 guard scoping) and its rework (GBL-103 tc-% slug scoping + iss107 cleanup + T060 lint), db_integration_test.zig's TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 -- the exact original #357 symptom -- STILL fail under standard `zig build test-integration` execution (which runs ~24 integration test binaries concurrently against one shared bpm_test database), even though every individual binary passes cleanly in isolation.

Root cause: tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig's TC-ISS503-01/02/03 deliberately bypass the normal migration-runner gating (by design -- see the file's own header comment, which explains this is necessary to test GBL-084's raw SQL/guard behavior independent of whether it has already been recorded as applied globally). They open their own direct pg.Conn, BEGIN a transaction they manage themselves, and either (a) INSERT a LEGACY_RLS tenant row and assert the raw GBL-084 guard fires (TC-ISS503-01), or (b) issue `UPDATE public.tenant SET storage_mode = 'SCHEMA' WHERE storage_mode = 'LEGACY_RLS'` -- an UNQUALIFIED, TABLE-WIDE update affecting every LEGACY_RLS row in public.tenant, not just rows this test owns -- then run GBL-084's raw, UNSCOPED guard/DDL (`readGbl084Sql()` + `conn.simpleQuery()`), then unconditionally ROLLBACK (TC-ISS503-02/03). GBL-084's own guard clause (migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql, lines ~32-34) was never modified by either GBL-102 or GBL-103 -- those later migrations only narrow the guard used by the NORMAL migration-runner path (src/db/migrations.zig's Migrations.run(), gated by schema_migrations); TC-ISS503-01/02/03 do not go through that path at all, so GBL-102/103's scoping has zero effect on them.

Since `zig build test-integration` runs this binary concurrently with db_integration_test.zig's binary (both depend on the same shared clean_test_db step but execute as separate OS processes against the same live bpm_test database), TC-ISS503-02/03's table-wide UPDATE and raw guard re-execution against public.tenant can interleave with db_integration_test.zig's own TestHarness.init() calls (which trigger the gated Migrations.run() path, re-evaluating GBL-102/GBL-103's guard against current live tenant state) at exactly the moments this rework was trying to protect. TEST-RUNNER confirmed via schema_migrations timestamp forensics that GBL-084/102/103's applied_at rows are unchanged across a failing run (ruling out the gated migration path re-triggering the guard directly) -- the failure instead surfaces through db_integration_test.zig's own guard check observing tenant.storage_mode='LEGACY_RLS' rows that are transiently visible/contended due to TC-ISS503-02/03's own uncommitted table-wide UPDATE running concurrently in a separate session. Full suite otherwise healthy: 553/666 passed, 103 failed, 10 skipped, consistent with the established pre-existing-failure baseline; no new failures attributable to ISS-0100's own fix or its rework's 3 files (GBL-103, tools/lint_test_isolation.py, tests/integration/iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig).

This is a genuine, pre-existing test-isolation gap -- NOT introduced by ISS-0100's fix or its rework, and NOT fixable by further scoping GBL-102/GBL-103's guard (which only governs the gated migration-runner path, not TC-ISS503-01/02/03's deliberate raw-SQL bypass). ISS-0100's own fix and rework are independently verified correct and complete for their own scope; #357 cannot be considered fully closed until this separate, deeper concurrency issue is also resolved.
candidate_resolution: Two non-exclusive candidate fixes: (a) scope GBL-084's OWN raw guard clause (migrations/GBL-084_rls_removal.sql itself, or a further migration if in-place editing is unsafe per this project's established 'migrations don't re-run once recorded' convention) the same way GBL-102/GBL-103 scope the gated path's guard -- but this changes what TC-ISS503-01/02/03 are specifically testing (the RAW, unscoped guard), so the test file's own assertions would need to be updated in lockstep to still exercise real guard-blocking behavior meaningfully; (b) serialize test-integration-iss503 in build.zig so it never runs concurrently with any other binary that queries/relies on public.tenant.storage_mode state (e.g. make it depend on the completion of, or run after, the primary test-integration step rather than as an independent concurrent target) -- lower risk to test semantics but reduces parallelism and may need a broader look at which OTHER integration test binaries also do concurrent raw/direct-connection mutations of shared global tables (this may not be the only file with this pattern). Needs its own WF-03 scoping decision; not part of ISS-0100's fix or its rework.
